title: Lifecycle — upgrades, migrations, and the failure that is silent
description: State continuity follows app_id. A fresh deploy where an upgrade belonged produces a working instance, empty state and a valid attestation — so the panels that matter here count guard refusals, not errors.

panels.title: Upgrades that changed app_id
panels.description: Must be zero. A non-zero value means a holder's encrypted volume is already unreachable — and the instance is healthy and attesting correctly, which is why this needs its own panel rather than showing up in an error rate.

panels.title: Fresh deploys refused over a running instance
panels.description: The I9 guard firing. Non-zero is *good* — it means something tried to create where an instance existed and was stopped. A sustained rate means a caller is repeatedly taking the wrong path.

panels.title: Migrations awaiting a holder
panels.description: Not an error. An instance parked here is indistinguishable from a slow migration until somebody looks — which is the whole reason it is surfaced rather than only returned.

panels.title: Migration outcomes
panels.description: Tri-state on purpose: complete / failed / needs_holder_action. A boolean would have forced an app that must ask its owner something to guess or fail.
